open_points.subject: owner authentication
open_points.text: Reaches the kernel through the agent channel with the owner's token.
open_points.question: Where is the owner's token configured, how is it distinguished from an agent token, and what validation, rotation and revocation rules apply to it?
options: A separately configured owner bearer token
An identity assertion supplied by the reverse proxy
The same token registry as agents with an owner role
open_points.default_guess: Use a separately configured owner token in protected installation configuration and validate it in constant time on every request.

open_points.subject: platform manifest authority
open_points.text: Microservices — known only as records of the platform manifest.
open_points.question: Who controls the manifest, how does the kernel obtain it, and is its operation metadata trusted or validated against another authority?
options: The installation supplies a trusted local manifest
A platform service supplies a signed manifest
The kernel reads manifests from named repositories
open_points.default_guess: Treat an installation-supplied local manifest as trusted configuration.

open_points.subject: submission of outside material
open_points.text: Their material stays at a microservice's own intake until the owner or an agent submits it.
open_points.question: What concrete action submits intake material, what input identifies it, and is the submission made to the microservice or to a flow?
options: Call the microservice intake API outside the kernel
Run a flow with an intake-record identifier
Invoke a dedicated kernel submission action
open_points.default_guess: Run a flow with a scalar identifier for material already held by the microservice.

open_points.subject: operation effect classification
open_points.text: Effect classes are `read`, `draft-write`, `state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`.
open_points.question: Which actor or record assigns an operation its effect class, and which trusted fact prevents an agent from proposing a harmful operation as `read`?
options: The trusted platform manifest declares the class
The proposed binding declares it and the owner accepts it
The kernel derives it from the HTTP request
open_points.default_guess: Require the trusted manifest operation record to declare the effect class and pin it with the binding.

open_points.subject: current contract version
open_points.text: the first contract of a new slot name creates the slot
open_points.question: When another contract version is authored for an existing slot, what makes that version the slot's current contract version, and what happens to the prior version's activation?
options: The new contract becomes current automatically
The owner explicitly activates a contract version
Every contract version remains independently current
open_points.default_guess: Make the newly authored contract version current automatically and leave old activations only for pinned runs.

open_points.subject: trial case contents
open_points.text: add a trial case
open_points.question: What fields constitute a trial case, especially the expected result or assertion against which an implementation passes?
options: Input values plus exact expected outputs
Input values plus output-schema conformance only
Input values plus explicit assertions and expected failure
open_points.default_guess: Store typed inputs and exact expected typed outputs or an explicitly expected failure.

open_points.subject: manual trial scope
open_points.text: try an implementation | agent | trial evidence per case
open_points.question: Does `try` execute the whole active corpus, selected existing cases, a supplied provisional case, or some combination?
options: Run the whole active corpus
Run explicitly selected corpus cases
Run supplied inputs without changing the corpus
open_points.default_guess: Run the whole active corpus and return evidence for every case.

open_points.subject: corpus growth and existing verdicts
open_points.text: the trial case every later implementation must pass
open_points.question: When a case is added, are existing admission verdicts recomputed or invalidated, and may the currently activated implementation continue running if it has not passed the enlarged corpus?
options: Keep the current activation but invalidate its verdict
Re-test all implementations and deactivate a failing current one
Apply new cases only to subsequently submitted implementations
open_points.default_guess: Keep the current activation, invalidate stale verdicts, and require a new whole-corpus verdict before any later activation or rollback.

open_points.subject: rollback eligibility after corpus growth
open_points.text: it must already hold an `admitted` verdict over the current corpus — rollback runs no admission
open_points.question: How can an older implementation acquire a verdict over a corpus enlarged after its last admission if rollback is forbidden to run admission?
options: Adding a case automatically evaluates every stored implementation
An implementation can be resubmitted to refresh its verdict
Rollback performs admission despite this sentence
open_points.default_guess: Allow resubmission of the existing implementation identity to run admission over the current corpus before rollback.

open_points.subject: capture of a failed execution
open_points.text: capture a failed execution into the trial corpus
open_points.question: Which failed executions are eligible, and how is a failed run record converted into a case with a pass condition when the execution produced no valid output?
options: Capture only failed function-node inputs with a separately supplied expected output
Capture the inputs and require merely that execution no longer fails
Capture the inputs and the original failure as an expected failure
open_points.default_guess: Limit capture to failed function nodes and require the caller to supply the expected typed output.

open_points.subject: flow run inputs
open_points.text: run a flow | owner, agent | a run of the flow's active version, with outputs
open_points.question: How are a flow's scalar input ports declared, and what request payload supplies and classifies their values when a run starts?
options: The flow version declares named typed input ports
Inputs are parameters of designated source nodes
Flows have no caller inputs and obtain everything from service reads
open_points.default_guess: Have each flow version declare named typed value inputs supplied in the run request.

open_points.subject: flow run outputs
open_points.text: with outputs
open_points.question: How are flow outputs selected and named, and what is returned when some independent branches succeed while another branch fails or waits?
options: The flow declares named output ports and returns only when all required outputs settle
Every terminal node is an output
Return partial outputs together with per-output status
open_points.default_guess: Require declared named outputs and return their values or individual unavailable/failure statuses.

open_points.subject: overall run verdict
open_points.text: a failed node stops its dependants
open_points.question: What terminal or resting status does the run receive when independent branches have different outcomes, and when is the run considered `succeeded` or `failed`?
options: Any failed required node makes the run failed
Only failure of a declared output dependency makes the run failed
Expose a mixed terminal state
open_points.default_guess: Fail the run if any node required by a declared output fails; otherwise succeed after all required outputs settle.

open_points.subject: service failure categories
open_points.text: pending when a service is unreachable or an outcome unknown
open_points.question: Which HTTP, transport, timeout and validation outcomes count as `unreachable`, `outcome_unknown`, or an ordinary failed node, especially when the kernel cannot prove whether a request was received?
options: Classify by whether bytes may have reached the service
Use HTTP status and transport-error categories
Treat every effect transport failure as outcome unknown
open_points.default_guess: Use `outcome_unknown` when an effect may have reached the service, `unreachable` only when no request was sent, and fail on definitive responses or invalid output.

open_points.subject: cancelling an in-flight send
open_points.text: the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent
open_points.question: What happens if cancellation arrives while an operation request is already in flight, and how is its possibly applied outcome recorded?
options: Cancellation is allowed only between node executions
The in-flight request completes and is recorded before cancellation
Cancellation aborts the request and may create an unknown outcome
open_points.default_guess: Do not claim cancellation of an already-started send; record its result or unknown outcome, then prevent subsequent sends.

open_points.subject: trace-read failure
open_points.text: read a trace | owner, agent | trace records | —
open_points.question: What observable failure is returned for an unknown trace or run reference, or for a trace the caller cannot read?
options: Return an unknown-reference refusal
Return an empty result
Use the same inspect operation and failure rules
open_points.default_guess: Return an unknown-reference refusal.

open_points.subject: standing-approval eligibility
open_points.text: a `destructive` node or a version that is not active cannot be granted
open_points.question: May standing approvals be granted to `read` and `draft-write` nodes even though they do not normally ask, or only to `state-transition` and `external-effect` nodes?
options: Any non-destructive operation node
Only nodes that normally stop for approval
Only `state-transition` nodes
open_points.default_guess: Allow grants only for `state-transition` and `external-effect` nodes.

open_points.subject: grant lifetime across flow activation
open_points.text: grant a standing approval for a node of a flow's active version
open_points.question: When another version becomes active, does the old version's grant remain active, become inactive permanently, or become usable again if that version is reactivated?
options: Persist with the exact version and revive on reactivation
Revoke automatically when the version ceases to be active
Remain active but unusable while the version is inactive
open_points.default_guess: Retain the record but make it inactive permanently when its flow version is superseded.

open_points.subject: effect repetition
open_points.text: The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key and never repeats an effect without a fresh approval.
open_points.question: Does “never repeats” mean retrying the same effect attempt after uncertainty, or does it also prohibit later runs under a standing grant and repeated `draft-write` executions?
options: Only a resend of the same attempt needs fresh approval
Every repeated request needs fresh approval
Standing grants and draft writes are exceptions
open_points.default_guess: Interpret it as a resend of the same attempt after an unknown or failed delivery, not a later ordinary run.

open_points.subject: idempotency key contract
open_points.text: The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key
open_points.question: Where is idempotency support declared, which operation classes require it, where is the key placed in the request, and what scope determines key uniqueness?
options: The manifest operation declares a header and every write requires it
The accepted binding declares the request field
Only operations that advertise idempotency receive a key
open_points.default_guess: Require every non-read manifest operation to declare an idempotency header and generate a key unique per effect attempt.

open_points.subject: function file output
open_points.text: no filesystem beyond its input
open_points.question: How can a function produce a file output when it may not write beyond its input filesystem?
options: A dedicated writable output path is allowed
File bytes are emitted through the sandbox protocol
Functions cannot actually produce file outputs
open_points.default_guess: Provide a bounded dedicated writable output area that is not part of the general filesystem.

open_points.subject: flow boundary ports
open_points.text: A flow is an immutable, acyclic graph with three structural forms: an edge, a map of a node over a collection, and a guard on a declared closed value.
open_points.question: What graph objects represent the flow's own inputs and outputs, and how are they connected to node ports?
options: Explicit flow-input and flow-output boundary ports
Distinguished source and sink nodes
Implicit unconnected node ports
open_points.default_guess: Use explicit typed flow-input and flow-output boundary ports.

open_points.subject: map and guard semantics
open_points.text: a map of a node over a collection, and a guard on a declared closed value
open_points.question: What are the observable runtime results and failures of maps and guards, including ordering, per-item failure, a false guard and a guard value outside the closed set?
options: Fail-fast ordered map and skipped guarded branch
Collect per-item results and failures
Treat non-selected guards as absent outputs rather than skipped nodes
open_points.default_guess: Preserve input order, fail a mapped node on any item failure, and record non-selected guarded nodes as skipped.

open_points.subject: surface coverage
open_points.text: The kernel exposes one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel.
open_points.question: Which MCP operations expose add-trial-case, capture-failure, release-failed-run, rollback, propose-binding, compose-and-prove, and effect refusal, all of which are separate primary actions but absent from this fixed list?
options: They are modes of the listed generic operations
They are missing fixed MCP operations
Some primary actions are internal and not remotely callable
open_points.default_guess: Expose them as explicit fixed MCP operations, with approve carrying both approve and refuse decisions only if that input is stated.

open_points.subject: process crash and restart
open_points.text: The kernel is one process with one store and one writer.
open_points.question: What happens to running, awaiting and pending runs after a process crash or restart, particularly when a service request was in flight?
options: Recover stored runs and classify in-flight effects as unknown
Mark every nonterminal run failed on restart
Provide no restart guarantee and require operator repair
open_points.default_guess: Recover stored nonterminal runs and turn any indeterminate in-flight effect into `pending/outcome_unknown`.

open_points.subject: skipped-node traces
open_points.text: Every node execution writes one immutable trace record
open_points.question: Does a node skipped because its dependency failed or its guard was false receive a trace record, despite not executing?
options: Every graph node receives a trace record including `skipped`
Only attempted nodes receive trace records
Dependency skips are recorded only on the run
open_points.default_guess: Create one trace record for every graph node, including skipped nodes and the reason.

open_points.subject: classification of non-service values
open_points.text: Every value carries `open`, `business_confidential` or `personal_data`.
open_points.question: Who assigns the class of caller-supplied flow inputs, guard constants, zero-input function outputs and other values that do not originate in a binding response or inherit a function input class?
options: The flow contract declares each such class
The submitting actor declares it
All such values default to `open`
open_points.default_guess: Require the immutable flow or function contract to declare their classes and reject unclassified values.

open_points.subject: authoritative repositories
open_points.text: the platform manifest and the repositories alone
open_points.question: Which repositories are authoritative, what records must they contain, and how does a replacement agent locate and authenticate to them?
options: Function source and platform configuration repositories named by installation config
One kernel repository containing all non-record knowledge
Repositories are documentation only and not kernel dependencies
open_points.default_guess: Name the function-source and platform-configuration repositories explicitly in installation configuration.

open_points.subject: deterministic admission environment
open_points.text: Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus
open_points.question: Which Python and standard-library version, platform image and resource-limit semantics are pinned so the same implementation and corpus produce the same admission verdict after an environment upgrade?
options: Pin an immutable sandbox runtime digest in the verdict
Re-admit everything whenever the runtime changes
Treat determinism as applying only within one installation version
open_points.default_guess: Pin an immutable sandbox runtime digest in trial evidence and admission verdicts.

open_points.subject: photo acceptance pending state
open_points.text: it shows effect classes, the owner's approval on the exact input, the idempotency key and `pending`
open_points.question: Which event must put the photo-upload case into `pending`: an unreachable service or an effect with unknown outcome, and what subsequent resolution must the case demonstrate?
options: Unreachable service followed by resume
Unknown effect outcome followed by owner resolution
Either pending reason is acceptable
open_points.default_guess: Require an unknown effect outcome, owner resolution and the fresh-approval rule for any resend.

open_points.subject: acceptance environment
open_points.text: both cases pass against the real service instances
open_points.question: For the effectful photo case, are the required “real service instances” the disposable rigs mandated for effectful-flow rehearsal, or production-like persistent instances?
options: Disposable rigs implementing the real APIs
Production service instances
Either installation type
open_points.default_guess: Use disposable real implementations of the service APIs.

open_points.subject: negative acceptance inventory
open_points.text: each refusal of K-05 through K-09 is shown by a bounded negative case
open_points.question: What exact finite list of refusal conditions must be demonstrated, given that K-05 through K-09 contain both refusals and runtime states without enumerating a bounded catalogue?
options: Every refusal explicitly stated in the primary-actions table
A separately enumerated conformance matrix
One representative refusal per decision K-05 through K-09
open_points.default_guess: Create an explicit conformance matrix covering every stated refusal branch in those decisions and their primary actions.

open_points.subject: analysis disclosure in the second acceptance case
open_points.text: returns an analysis
open_points.question: What disclosure class does the third-party input and resulting analysis carry, and is the observable analysis returned as a value to the agent or only as digest and class?
options: Business-confidential data returned in full to the agent
Personal data returned only as digest and class
Open data returned in full
open_points.default_guess: Classify the case data and analysis as `business_confidential` so the agent can receive the analysis value.

open_points.subject: photo processing outside the kernel
open_points.text: the agent processes a photo itself, outside the kernel
open_points.question: How does the agent obtain and submit that photo without contradicting the rules that callers never receive files from the kernel and outside material remains at a service intake, and what disclosure class permits the agent to see it?
options: The agent accesses the intake service directly outside the kernel
The owner processes the file and supplies only derived values
No agent photo processing occurs in the acceptance flow
open_points.default_guess: Keep the agent away from the file and use declared service operations for all file processing and custody.

open_points.subject: open-question status
open_points.text: None.
open_points.question: How can the section declare no open questions while the owner-token model, manifest authority, trial oracle, run interface, effect-class authority and other product-boundary choices remain unspecified?
options: Answer these choices in State 0
Explicitly carry each named question to a later state
Remove the affected promises
open_points.default_guess: Answer the product-boundary choices in State 0 and explicitly carry only implementation details.
